narrative:
Over the past quarter century, Philadelphia's City Council has introduced a staggering 8,578 bills, shaping the city's laws and policies in countless ways. This comprehensive dataset spans an entire generation of council members, revealing trends and patterns that shed light on the city's priorities and challenges. From zoning regulations to transportation infrastructure, the legislative record is a treasure trove of insights into how city government works.

Some striking patterns emerge from this data. For instance, Council President Clarke has sponsored an impressive 775 bills over the years, but other council members have also made significant contributions to the legislative agenda. The most active issue areas – zoning (2,560 bills), planning (1,933 bills), and infrastructure (1,529 bills) – suggest that City Hall is deeply concerned with the physical development of the city. Meanwhile, the 99% pass rate for signed bills implies a relatively efficient and harmonious legislative process, although it's unclear what proportion of those bills were truly contentious or difficult to pass.

This wealth of data offers a unique opportunity for citizens to engage more deeply with their local government. By tracking legislation on Open Common Ground, Philadelphians can monitor the issues that matter most to them and hold elected officials accountable for their actions. With this information at hand, residents can make informed decisions about which candidates to support or how to organize around specific causes – a vital step towards creating positive change in their communities.
